title: AnyWork — Your local agents. Anywhere.
description: Continue your local Codex workspace from a browser or Android phone. Conversations, approvals, files and tools, connected to your own computer.
release: Open source. Runs on your computer.
headline:
Good work.
No fixed address.
intro: Keep Codex working on your computer. Continue the conversation, approve the next step, and check the result—from your browser or phone.
demoLabel: The conversation. And everything around it.
demoPrompt: Review the release page and polish the mobile experience.
demoReply: The layout now adapts to smaller screens. I also checked the download links and keyboard navigation.
changeText: The layout follows the screen. The context stays with you.
phonePrompt: Can you run the final checks?
phoneHint: Example approval · no command is executed
manifestoText: Pick up an existing chat, follow tool calls and subagents, review files, and keep the conversation moving. A workspace built for the way Codex works.
feature1Text: Stream replies, find earlier messages, steer running work and keep drafts between chats. Tools and subagents have their own place in the conversation.
feature2Text: Respond to an approval, inspect a change, or add an image with your own annotations. Browser notifications bring you back when the work needs attention.
feature3Text: Open files, documents, Git changes and a terminal beside your conversation. Each chat remembers its own set of tabs.
connectText: Stay on your local network, open an HTTPS tunnel, or connect over WireGuard. Manage each route independently from the desktop app.
lanText: Connect directly on a trusted LAN. Your device reaches the service running on your own computer.
tunnelText: Use a temporary Cloudflare address or configure your own domain. Temporary addresses can change when the tunnel restarts.
vpnText: Connect Android through your private WireGuard network, or configure a compatible TLS relay. Bring your own network or relay.
routeFoot: No mandatory AnyWork cloud relay. Model requests still go to your configured model provider. Third-party tunnels follow their own policies.
startTitle: From your desk to your pocket, in three steps.
step1Text: Install and sign into Codex on your computer. Open AnyWork, choose your workspace, and start the service.
step2Text: Use the local address or enable a tunnel in the manager. Keep the host computer awake and online.
step3Title: Pick up where you left off
step3Text: Open the address in your browser or Android app, enter your access key, and continue working.
downloadText: Install the manager on your computer. Take the workspace with you.
releaseLoading: Release packages are being prepared. View build status on GitHub.
androidNote: Android 8+ · Signed universal APK · Current WebView
faq1Q: Does the work run on my phone?
faq1A: No. Codex and its tools run on your host computer. Your phone or browser connects to that workspace. The host needs to stay awake and connected.
faq2Q: Can I continue an existing Codex chat?
faq2A: AnyWork discovers local history and uses supported local sharing interfaces to collaborate with a running desktop session. These interfaces depend on the installed Codex version and Unix platform. Windows uses CLI-backed chats. Read the compatibility notes before relying on desktop hot attach.
faq3A: No AnyWork account is required. You use an access key for your own host and your existing Codex login for model calls. Named tunnels and private relays need their own configuration.
faq4Q: What is included in this release?
faq4A: The included agent is Codex. Full goal operations need a compatible shared engine; the desktop follower can read and pause goals. Voice, cross-client native queue migration and notifications after the browser closes are not included. See the guide for the complete scope.

howTitle: Your work stays here. You can go anywhere.
howText: AnyWork connects your browser or Android app to Codex on your own computer. Your files, tools and working context stay with the host.
cliTitle: Prefer the terminal? That works too.
cliText: Run the same service from a portable package. Choose your workspace and connect with the Web client.
